title: Circled chip numbers sit apart in tmux and touch in ghostty
body: In the marking scenario, a prompt holding two chips and then typed text draws as `① ②  blah` in tmux at 80 × 28 and as `①②blah` in ghostty at font size 18, from the same key presses. The circled digits (U+2460 on) have East Asian ambiguous width, so coax and the terminal may disagree on whether a chip takes one column or two. The README scenario types a leading space to look right in ghostty. Nobody has checked which width coax gives a chip.
close_reason: Not a coax bug. The circled digits are East Asian ambiguous width. coax measures a chip with `unicode-width`, which counts ambiguous characters as one column, and ghostty draws them in one column, so the two agree and the prompt's cursor lands right. tmux 3.8 gives them two columns, which opens the gap after each chip in tmux only.
